Priority plan operations for navigating and managing priority plans.

This command group provides operations for working with priority plans:
  - current: View backlog items for the current priority plan
  - next: Navigate to the next priority plan
  - prev: Navigate to the previous priority plan
  - add: Associate a backlog item with a priority plan (child-owned)
  - remove: Clear priority plan association from a backlog item

Flags:
    --ignore-scheduler-down
      Ignore scheduler down warning/lockdown

  View backlog items for current priority plan
  zqk.test pplan current
  Add backlog item to priority plan
  zqk.test pplan add PRI-123 BLI-456
  Alternative positional syntax
  zqk.test pplan PRI-123 add BLI-456
  Remove backlog item from priority plan
  zqk.test pplan remove PRI-123 BLI-456

Usage:
  zqk.test object pplan [flags]
  zqk.test object pplan [command]

Available Commands:
  add         Add backlog item(s) to a priority plan (child-owned priority_plan_ref)
  current     View backlog items for the current priority plan
  next        Navigate to the next priority plan
  prev        Navigate to the previous priority plan
  remove      Remove backlog item association(s) from a priority plan

Flags:
      --columns string          Override column widths for table output (format: field:width)
  -f, --format string           Output format (table, json, jsonl, yaml, csv, json-rpc, stream, agent-prompt, semantic-link) (default "table")
      --ignore-scheduler-down   Ignore scheduler down warning/lockdown
  -o, --output string           Write output to file
  -q, --quiet                   Suppress non-essential output
      --timeout duration        Timeout for command execution (0 = auto-calculate)
  -v, --verbose                 Verbose output

Global Flags:
      --allow-degraded   Allow scheduler-dependent commands to run when scheduler daemon is not running
      --internal         Elevated access mode for built-in and internal kinds (requires Enterprise license or zqk-admin)

Use "zqk.test object pplan [command] --help" for more information about a command.
